content:
Bloomberg today reports that Apple is about to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" rental program for hardware. The program will allow users to purchase new Apple products via a monthly subscription, but sources indicate there is a limitation, hoping it won't ultimately come true.

"Apple Upgrade" will make more expensive products more accessible, but reportedly excludes entry-level models

Affected by the current AI-driven memory chip crisis, most Apple products have seen price increases recently.

This autumn, this trend will further intensify, with newly released iPhone and Apple Watch models also expected to see price hikes. Higher-end iPhone Ultra and MacBook Ultra products will also debut for the first time.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple's response is to launch a brand-new "Apple Upgrade" hardware monthly subscription option.

Gurman stated that this option will launch next week on Apple's online store and retail stores, applicable to the purchase of related products.

Before the final details are confirmed, I think making Apple products more accessible in this way is a good approach.

Apple Upgrade will be entirely voluntary, so any user who wants to purchase products directly can still do so. But given the recent wave of price hikes, adding more options seems like a natural move.

My only concern is the scope of eligible hardware. Gurman pointed out that some devices will not be included in Apple Upgrade, including "Apple Watch SE, entry-level iPad, iPhone 16, and MacBook Neo".

It would be a shame if Apple doesn't allow users to purchase its most affordable products through the rental program.

Imagine this: you've always felt Apple products were beyond your budget, but with this new program, you could own a MacBook Neo for just $20 per month. In this case, Apple Upgrade is expected to bring a large number of new users to the Apple ecosystem.

I understand Apple's idea of wanting to encourage users to purchase higher-priced products. But limiting Apple Upgrade to specific hardware seems to complicate the program unnecessarily and weaken its impact.

What are your thoughts on the Apple Upgrade program? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
